title: Common gate
description: A common-gate stage: the input drives the source, the gate is AC-grounded, and the output is taken at the drain. It presents a low input resistance (a current-mode input, so it is the classic input matching / current-buffer stage) and a non-inverting voltage gain $A_v = (g_m + g_{mb} + g_{ds})*par(R_{load}, 1/g_{ds})$ equal in magnitude to a common source. Its current transfer from source to drain is essentially unity, so it passes an input current to the load with a low input impedance. Both figures carry the source-body generator: the input drives the source, so $g_{mb}$ acts in parallel with $g_m$ rather than as a second-order correction. The input resistance is the DIVIDED form $R_{in} = (R_{load} + r_o)/(1 + (g_m + g_{mb})*r_o)$ — the drain load appears at the source divided by the device's own loop gain, which is why the popular $1/(g_m + g_{mb})$ shorthand reads low here. The load resistor returns to $V_{DD}$ and carries the whole branch current, so the drain sits at $V_{out} = V_{DD} - I_{bias}*R_{load}$. The device source sits at the input DC level $V_{in}$, so its givens declare $V_{DS} = V_{out} - V_{in}$ and $V_{SB} = V_{in}$ (body grounded); a table with no $g_{mb}$ column leaves these equations unresolved rather than quietly dropping the term. The input (source) is held at $V_{in}$. The gate is a port because its bias is not drawn: it has to sit one device $V_{GS}$ above $V_{in}$, the voltage a bias line outside the sheet supplies. Nothing is solved.

params.name: V_in
params.note: input (source) DC level, stated by whatever drives the stage. The gate bias is not a parameter here: it is this level plus the device's vgs

params.name: R_load
params.note: load resistor from the drain to VDD: sets the gain, and with the branch current the drain DC level

params.name: Av_target
params.note: DC gain target: 10 (20 dB) into the 50 kOhm load, the range of a common-gate input or current-buffer stage, where the low input resistance is the point and the gain comes second. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: GBW_target
params.note: unity-gain bandwidth target into the 2 pF load plus the parasitic estimate: ten megahertz is the range of a single stage biased at tens of microamps. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: cdd_per_um
params.note: an estimate from simulation on sky130, 0.3 to 0.4 fF per micron of drain width; no table carries a drain capacitance column

params.name: gm_id
params.note: lower gm/ID raises gm, so it lowers Rin (better matching) at the cost of headroom

equations.name: V_out
equations.note: output (drain) DC level: the supply less the drop the branch current makes across the load. The givens write the same level with I_bias, the current they size the device at, because the givens are evaluated before any equation

equations.name: Rin
equations.note: low-frequency input resistance looking into the source, with the drain load carried through: (R_load + ro)/(1 + (gm + gmb)*ro). The finite ro couples the load back to the source, so a heavier R_load raises Rin — the 1/(gm + gmb) shorthand drops that and reads low (on a sky130 tt realization of this stage, simulated at a 0.6 V drain-source bias, it gave 4.21 k against a measured 4.73 k)

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: the resistance this stage presents at its drain: the load resistor in parallel with the device output resistance. It holds for an ideal driving source; a real source impedance degenerates the device and raises it

equations.name: Av
equations.note: non-inverting gain: the source drive acts through gm, the source-body generator gmb, and the device's own gds in parallel, into the load paralleled with ro

equations.name: Cout
equations.note: the load plus what the device adds at the output, its drain junction and gate-drain overlap, at cdd_per_um per micron of its width, so a resized device carries a proportionate estimate. The 2.5 µm device the defaults size on the sky130 tables adds 1.0 fF, simulated, and 0.89 fF by this estimate; wiring comes on top, so refine from extraction

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: thermal density referred to the input, the source: the channel's noise current (vnth_m*gm) and the load resistor's 4kT/R_load both land at the drain, and the source reaches the drain through gm + gmb + gds, the transconductance of the gain, so both refer back through that rather than through gm. Referred by gm alone, and without the resistor, the row read 18 % above the simulated density. A common-gate input also passes the source's own noise, which is set outside this stage

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the one branch these equations model; the source that sets it is outside the stage. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no check reads it

checks.note: gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data

the resistance looking into the source must meet the input-resistance budget. This is what a common gate is usually infeasible on: closing it takes proportionally more gm, i.e. more current, not a different topology
actual GBW into CL plus the parasitic estimate
